_interpretation: Beethoven reading of 'The Neighbour' for solo piano, after the fugue of Op. 110 (the model of this design).
Reproduce: performance/beethoven_piano/render.sh (perform.py --target piano, then render_piano.py; options in render.sh).
Tempo: fugue steady at 78, a breath of broadening at the half cadence (17), the false-dawn stretto presses to 82, the dim7 slide broadens to 64 into the re-struck fermata chord and the general pause.

Arioso dolente (30-34): rubato, 50 moving on to 54 through each rising figure and yielding at the long notes; a held breath and a broadening into the 7-6 peak (32:1); easing through the 4-3 and the German-sixth pivot down to 40, then a long breath.
Fuga inversa (35-45): 'poi a poi di nuovo vivente', 60 growing to 76, weight on the A-minor cadence, a breath before the deceptive F.
Pedal section (46-53): one long crescendo from p misterioso to the peak at 53:1, in two unbroken ramps (slow to 50:1, steep to 53:1), pressing forward to 78 and broadening to 64 into the V fermata.
Apotheosis (55-66): Largamente at 70, broadening to 64 through the tune's peak (f, 60:4), a breath before c''-d'' (63:1), dying away to 48 and a long final fermata.

Dynamics: p at the start, wide arc from pp to fff; subito cuts at 18:1 (p after the mf half cadence, so the false dawn has room to grow), 24:3 (the bare fifth that turns minor), 30:1 (pp arioso after the general pause), 46:1 (p misterioso). Climax I stays at ff- (6.3-6.4); the long crescendo reaches 7.6 at the C6 (52:3) and fff only on the complete C7 (53:1-53:3), so Climax II is the loudest moment of the piece; the V fermata is held at 7.6. The apotheosis peaks at f (5.8), below both climaxes: a glow, not a third climax.

Voicing: every subject, answer and augmentation entry brought out (subject/answer +12, cf +9, cs +3, free -5, the README demo's validated voicing); whenever an entry overlaps the end of the previous one, that tail recedes to +3 (soprano at 5:1, alto at 9:1, bass at 13:1, tenor at 22:1, bass at 37:1, tenor at 41:1; the soprano's G-flat entry is voiced to 26:3, where the first liquidation head enters), so each new head is heard; at 50:3 the alto's S2 and the tenor's S1 recede to +9 so the soprano's diminution heads lead the three speeds, and the held notes between diminution heads are free (soprano g'' at 52:1, alto e'' at 52:3) and the tenor's S1 recedes to +3 as it breaks off (52:1), so the alto's head on E (52:1) and the soprano's C6 (52:3) are heard at a dynamic where every voice is near the velocity ceiling; the whole tune in the apotheosis (55:1-63:2, including the d'' that answers its open c'') is voiced +14, a cantus firmus glowing over the triple counterpoint; the bass answer under it (59) gets +9, so it is heard without covering the tune; the soprano's C-B sigh in the pivot bar (34) keeps +6; the four liquidation heads (26:3-28:1) all enter over held notes and get +5 only, so Climax I stays below Climax II; the tenor's lament lead-in (46-47) is voiced as a countersubject over the bass pedal.

Pedal: only where the texture is chordal: the fermata chord (29), the arioso each harmony (30-34, per beat in 31, the passing and neighbour notes left dry), the V fermata (53:4), the coda over the tolling tonic pedal (63-66, each harmony, neighbour notes dry). None in the contrapuntal apotheosis 55-62 (CS2's eighths would blur).
Not modelled by the engine: una corda (the arioso and the start of the inversion are simply pp), sostenuto (the F2 pedal of 46-50 is held by the key).
